Compute Screener

Methodology

GPU prices are currently based on Compute Rental Prices and will transition to Compute Futures Prices as the market matures (see below).

Compute Screener, built and run by @RenshuBTC, publishes a daily GPU Price Index for each GPU family and a daily Token Price Index for each AI company, calculated automatically by the rules below and recomputable from the published data.

GPU Price IndexToken Price Index
MeasuresThe on-demand rental price of a GPU family at neo-cloud providers and GPU marketplacesThe posted API price of a company's models, weighted by their usage
UnitUSD / GPU-hourUSD / 1M tokens, at a mix of 87% cache reads, 12% input and 1% output
DayCalendar day in US Central TimeUTC day
UpdatedEvery minute; provisional during the day, final when it endsOnce a day, shortly after the day ends
Version4.2, from 2026-10-282.0, from 2026-10-28

Compute Rental Prices and Compute Futures Prices

The site's GPU prices are Compute Rental Prices: the GPU Price Index below, from the on-demand prices providers post. They will move to Compute Futures Prices, exchange-traded contracts on GPU rental, once that market is deep enough. In October 2026 futures trade only on H100 and B200 (perpetual contracts, most volume on one exchange), and the futures CME Group and ICE announced are not trading yet. Each GPU's page shows every exchange's last price and 24-hour volume under Compute Futures Prices; they enter no index. The switch will be announced here at least 14 days ahead (Governance).

GPU Price Index

Indices for H100, H200, A100, B200, B300, MI300X and RTX PRO 6000, from 2026-10-28 L40S and RTX A6000, and from 2026-10-30 RTX 6000 Ada, L40 and RTX 4090. A GPU is added once a whole day of collection prices it at 5 providers; RTX 5090 and RTX A4000 are collected until then. GPUs without a shown index are on Every GPU, as posted. Hyperscalers are not in the index: each GPU's page lists providers outside it (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, Akamai, Koyeb, Packet, Northflank, Fireworks AI, Thunder Compute, DeepInfra, Replicate, Baseten, Lightning AI, Beam, fal, Exoscale, Atlantic.Net, Hugging Face, IBM Cloud, Novita AI, Oblivus, FriendliAI, Seeweb and, from 2026-11-01, SaladCloud) under Other Posted Prices, as posted, not standardized; Seeweb posts in euros, converted at the ECB rate of the day and shown with its euro price, before VAT as Seeweb lists its prices. Each price is converted to its GPU's benchmark contract:

IndexBenchmark contract
  1. Collect. Posted on-demand prices are read from each provider's API or pricing page: the Vast.ai, Lium, RunPod, Akash and Shadeform marketplaces every minute, the Verda, Scaleway and Vultr catalogues every 5 minutes, other price lists every 30 minutes, and CoreWeave's (which refuses the live collector's network) several times a day by the scheduled update. The index is recalculated every minute. An offer's price for the day is the average of its readings with capacity, so a source read more often does not weigh more. Sources are rate cards, every ask on Vast.ai and Lium, Akash's average ask, and smaller clouds through Shadeform's public catalog; no cloud is read through two sources for the same GPU. Euro prices are converted at the European Central Bank's rate of the day. From 2026-10-30, offers located in Russia, Belarus, Iran or North Korea, countries under broad international sanctions, are not collected. If the live collection stops, the scheduled update reads every source several times a day.
  2. Filter. Where a source shows capacity, a provider counts for a GPU only if one of its offers had capacity at some collection that day; then all its posted prices count, so a sell-out does not read as a price change. Marketplace asks more than 2× from their marketplace's median, and prices more than 2.5× from the GPU's historical reference, are left out. A marketplace counts only with at least 3 usable asks from at least 2 hosts.
  3. Check. A provider's price that moves more than 35% from its 14-day median is held out until the new level lasts 3 days, unless the market moved with it (net of the median move of at least 3 other sources, under 35%). A move shared by most clouds in one catalog and by no other source is that catalog's error and stays held.
  4. Standardize. Each price is divided by factors for how it differs from the benchmark: form factor and memory, GPUs per rental, region and CPU. Factors are estimated weekly over 28 days from providers that price both configurations the same day, with comparisons from at least 2 providers (5 matched groups for region and CPU); without them, a price with another form factor or memory is left out and other differences are not adjusted. The factors for GPUs per rental, region and CPU come from the first seven GPUs (H100 to RTX PRO 6000) and apply to every GPU, so adding a GPU does not change them. A GPU added later is one card with one form factor and memory; a listing with other memory (an RTX 4090 modified to 48 GB) is left out.
  5. Average. Each provider's prices are averaged, so a provider counts once. A provider with no price on a day is carried for up to 7 days, moved by the other providers' average change.
  6. Chain. The index moves by the geometric mean of the price changes of providers priced both today and on the last published day:index today = index last × geometric mean of (provider average today ÷ provider average last)Itoday=Ilast×(∏i=1npˉi,todaypˉi,last)1/nI_{\text{today}} = I_{\text{last}} \times \left( \prod_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\bar{p}_{i,\text{today}}}{\bar{p}_{i,\text{last}}} \right)^{1/n}Itoday​=Ilast​×(i=1∏n​pˉ​i,last​pˉ​i,today​​)1/nwhere pˉi\bar{p}_ipˉ​i​ is the average price of provider iii and nnn the number of providers priced on both days. Both averages use today's factors, so neither a recalibration nor providers joining or leaving move the index.
FactorCurrent values

Publication. A value needs at least 5 matched providers, 3 of them priced that day, so none weighs more than 20%. A new provider counts after 14 days of collection (the 15 added by version 4.1 counted at once). For a GPU added later, providers priced in its first 14 days count at once, and its index starts at the cross-section average on its first day with 5 providers. After 7 days without a published value, the index restarts at the cross-section average (the mean of provider averages, extremes clipped). Also published daily in /data/index.json: the cross-section average, the quartiles of provider averages and monthly averages.

History. Live from 2026-10-23. Before that, H100 and A100 are daily from 2025-11-07, rebuilt with this method from SkyPilot's open price catalog (5 to 8 providers a day); earlier, and for the other GPUs, weekly: GetDeploying's on-demand median across providers, in weeks with at least 5. Each earlier series is scaled to meet the later one, so a change of source does not move the index. A GPU added later (L40S and RTX A6000 on 2026-10-28; RTX 6000 Ada, L40 and RTX 4090 on 2026-10-30) is joined to that weekly history on its first day, unless the week is more than 25% from the median of the three weeks before.

Token Price Index

One index for each AI company in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index chart (version 4.3.2, October 2026) whose models are used through OpenRouter: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Meta, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, DeepSeek, Z.ai, Xiaomi, StepFun, MiniMax, Mistral, Reflection AI, NVIDIA and Thinking Machines. A day's value is what the company's paid tokens cost that day at the mix agents send: its models' prices weighted by their tokens:index = Σ (tokens × price) ÷ Σ tokensI=∑jqj Pj∑jqjI = \frac{\sum_{j} q_j \, P_j}{\sum_{j} q_j}I=∑j​qj​∑j​qj​Pj​​where qjq_jqj​ is model jjj's tokens that day and PjP_jPj​ is its price at the mix.

GLM 5.3's price at the mix: 0.87 × $0.26 cache read + 0.12 × $1.40 input + 0.01 × $4.40 output = $0.4382 per 1M tokens.

  • Tokens: each model's daily prompt and completion tokens in OpenRouter's daily rankings of the top 50 models.
  • The mix. A model's price is its posted price for the mix of tokens OpenRouter measured in agentic use in September 2026, "roughly 87% cached, 12% novel prompt, 1% output" (OpenRouter, Inferred 03, 8 October 2026):price = 0.87 × cache read price + 0.12 × input price + 0.01 × output priceP=0.87 Pcache+0.12 Pin+0.01 PoutP = 0.87\,P_{\text{cache}} + 0.12\,P_{\text{in}} + 0.01\,P_{\text{out}}P=0.87Pcache​+0.12Pin​+0.01Pout​A cache read is a prompt token served from the provider's prompt cache; a model without a cache price has no cache discount (cache read = input). Cache writes are not counted. The mix is fixed, so the index moves only with prices and with which models are used. Every token price on the site in USD / 1M tokens is at this mix, except break-even throughput, which uses the list price.
  • Prices: the company's own posted standard prices (no batch, priority or long-context pricing), read from its endpoint on OpenRouter shortly after each UTC day ends; if the endpoint is briefly missing, the price read up to 3 days before is kept. A price that depends on the hour counts at the rate in force most of the week (DeepSeek bills twice its base rate on weekdays 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC).
  • Companies that sell no API of their own (NVIDIA, Thinking Machines, Reflection AI): their models are at the median posted price of the providers serving them on OpenRouter, each at its standard tier, ranked at the mix.
  • Models that count: paid text models. Free variants, batch tiers, embedding, image and safety models, and OpenAI's and Google's open-weight releases (gpt-oss, Gemma) are left out. An open-weight model from a company that sells its own API counts only while the company itself serves it.
  • Days without a countable model: the company is priced at its last model weights (its models' shares on the last day it had some) at that day's prices, marked in the data (c: the day the weights are from).
  • Coverage: a value is published only when models with a known price carry at least 80% of the tokens that count, or of the carried weights.
  • List price: version 1's blend, kept beside each value for comparison:list price = (3 × input price + output price) ÷ 4Plist=3 Pin+Pout4P_{\text{list}} = \frac{3\,P_{\text{in}} + P_{\text{out}}}{4}Plist​=43Pin​+Pout​​
  • Estimated spend on OpenRouter (below): what each company's paid models in the daily top 50 cost at its posted prices and the mix, Σ tokens × price ÷ 106 USD a day, with the last 30 days' total and a year at that rate (× 365 ÷ 30). Only those models count, so these are floors, not revenue; — when none of its models was in the top 50 that day.
Estimated spendLast dayLast 30 daysA year at that rate

History. Daily from 2025-01-01, from OpenRouter's rankings dataset (/data/legacy/openrouter_rankings.json.gz), at each day's prices, in this order: the company's own dated records (DeepSeek's change log and price notices, Xiaomi's update log, Moonshot AI's model list and pricing pages, StepFun's and Alibaba's notices, Google's and xAI's pricing pages and release notes, OpenAI's model pages, changelog and deprecations, Anthropic's release notes and pricing page, Meta's model pages); the dated history at llm-prices.com by Simon Willison; prices read on version 1's live days (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-27); otherwise today's price, assumed unchanged. A missing cache price is today's cache discount applied to the day's input price; without either, the price is unknown. Where a company's records date which versions it served, they decide which count (a version served free does not); otherwise an open-weight model it serves today counts from its release, and a day is left empty when versions of unknown service or price carry over 20% of tokens. Before 2026-08-17 DeepSeek is priced at the standard rates of its price announcements (its 2025 night discount covered 8 hours of 24), and from then at its off-peak base rates; a model a company's records show it never served, as DeepSeek's R1 distillations, does not count. The history was completed on 2026-10-30 with dated prices found for the models it had priced at today's price or not at all (/data/legacy/restatements.json).

Every AI model. Every AI model lists every model OpenRouter prices for text output, read from each model's public endpoint list several times a day, by the rules above: its maker's own price (or announced price, where the maker's records say it serves a model OpenRouter lists only at other providers), else the providers' median at the mix, with the lowest provider beside it. Free variants, batch and flex tiers, routers and non-text models are left out; open-weight models are in, at the providers' median. Prices that cannot be read in a run are kept up to 3 days. Not an index: no usage weights.

Listing

A GPU or company is listed once it has a price, a month of history and a value for each of its 1-day, 1-week and 1-month changes. A change is measured against the value that many days earlier or, where the history has none that day (weekly history, a missing day), against the straight-line interpolation between the nearest values before and after it, if at most 14 days apart (the change cell says so on hover). DeepSeek is always listed. MI300X is collected but not published: fewer than 5 providers price it.

Price trend

The Compute and Tokens tabs list GPUs and companies by the strength of their 13-week price trend, strongest first, up or down.

  1. Prices. The index on 13 dates a week apart, ending with the latest (provisional during the day).
  2. Line. A least-squares line through the logarithms of those prices:ln(price) = intercept + slope × weekln⁡pk=a+b k+ek,k=0,1,…,12\ln p_k = a + b\,k + e_k, \qquad k = 0, 1, \ldots, 12lnpk​=a+bk+ek​,k=0,1,…,12where pkp_kpk​ is the price in week kkk, bbb is the fitted slope and eke_kek​ are the residuals. The slope is the trend's speed, shown per month:speed per month = e^(slope × 52 ÷ 12) − 1speed=e52 b/12−1\text{speed} = e^{52\,b/12} - 1speed=e52b/12−1
  3. Score. The slope over its standard error (its t-statistic): large when the price moved steadily one way.score = slope ÷ standard error of the slopet=bSE⁡(b)t = \frac{b}{\operatorname{SE}(b)}t=SE(b)b​SE⁡(b)=∑kek2 / (13−2)∑k(k−6)2\operatorname{SE}(b) = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_k e_k^2 \,/\, (13 - 2)}{\sum_k (k - 6)^2}}SE(b)=∑k​(k−6)2∑k​ek2​/(13−2)​​

Strength. Strong: a score of 4 or more; moderate: 2 to 4; weak: under 2, which noise alone often makes. The arrow shows the direction. Less than 12 weeks of history: no score, listed last.

Why this measure. From 24 January to 26 September 2026, the GPU with the strongest score kept its direction over the next 4 weeks in 29 of 36 weeks (following it gained 2.3% on average); the GPU with the largest 1-week change kept it in 11 of 26 (following it lost 1.1%). One year of six GPUs is a small sample: evidence, not a forecast. The Tokens tab uses the same measure, tested on GPUs only.

Break-even throughput and gross margin

Each model's page shows its break-even throughput on each GPU: the tokens per second one GPU must generate, sold at the model's list price (3 input : 1 output, as in the Token Price Index), to cover the GPU's rental price today; each GPU's page shows it for every model in the token index. The gross margin calculator on each model's page compares an hour's revenue with the rental price.

  1. Revenue per GPU-hour. An hour's tokens at the model's list price:revenue per GPU-hour = throughput × 3,600 × list price ÷ 1,000,000R=3600×T×P106R = \frac{3600 \times T \times P}{10^{6}}R=1063600×T×P​ And the other way, the throughput that earns a revenue:throughput = revenue per GPU-hour × 1,000,000 ÷ (3,600 × list price)T=106×R3600×PT = \frac{10^{6} \times R}{3600 \times P}T=3600×P106×R​
  2. Gross profit per GPU-hour. Revenue less the GPU's rental price:gross profit per GPU-hour = revenue per GPU-hour − GPU rental priceG=R−CG = R - CG=R−C
  3. Gross margin. Gross profit as a share of revenue:gross margin = gross profit ÷ revenue per GPU-hourM=GR=1−CRM = \frac{G}{R} = 1 - \frac{C}{R}M=RG​=1−RC​
  4. Break-even throughput. Where revenue equals the rental price:break-even throughput = GPU rental price × 1,000,000 ÷ (3,600 × list price)TBE=106×C3600×PT_{\text{BE}} = \frac{10^{6} \times C}{3600 \times P}TBE​=3600×P106×C​

where TTT is throughput in tokens per second per GPU, PPP is the model's list price in USD per 1M tokens, CCC is the GPU's rental price in USD per GPU-hour (its GPU Price Index today), RRR and GGG are revenue and gross profit in USD per GPU-hour, and MMM is gross margin.

Example. At a rental price of $3.00 per GPU-hour and a list price of $1.00 per 1M tokens, break-even throughput is 833 tokens per second per GPU. At 5,000 tokens per second, revenue is $18.00 per GPU-hour, gross profit $15.00 and gross margin 83%.

Throughput is entered by the visitor or worked out from an entered revenue; Compute Screener does not measure it. It counts input and output tokens together at 3 : 1, depends on model, GPU, serving software, batch size and context length, and for many GPUs is the deployment's tokens per second divided by its GPUs. A company's reported revenue can rest on another mix, cache hits and discounts.

Limits. List prices are the base input and output rates, without cache or batch discounts. The only cost counted is the GPU's rental price (no networking, storage, staff or idle time), at that throughput for the whole hour.

Reported figures are shown as reported, unverified: DeepSeek reported revenue of US$38 per GPU-hour for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at its off-peak ("valley") prices, from a cluster serving 155 trillion tokens a day (deployment Q&A, October 2026), without naming the GPUs.

Every value can be recomputed from these public files, kept for five years:

FileHolds
/data/readings/<day>.json.gzFrom 2026-10-28, every GPU price reading at every collection, with its time: each offer's price per GPU-hour as posted and whether it had capacity (summed, they give the day's records)
/data/records/<day>.json.gzEach offer read that day, with its source page, configuration and latest price, and how many readings it had with and without capacity and their sums
/data/trace/<day>.json.gzEach price used, with its factor, or left out, with the reason; provider averages, chain ratio and matched providers
/data/model.json, /data/stats.jsonStandardization factors and the comparisons behind them; validation references and imputation inputs
/data/index.json, /data/series.jsonLatest GPU values with their providers; full history
/data/token_trace/<day>.json.gz, /data/tokens.json, /data/token_series.jsonEach company's models, tokens, input, output and cache read prices and shares by day, with the day's full OpenRouter rankings and the posted prices of the chart's models; latest values; full history
/data/legacy/History inputs and joins: skypilot_daily.json, getdeploying_weekly.json, history_link.json, token_history.json, llm_prices.json, openrouter_rankings.json.gz (OpenRouter's daily rankings dataset from 2025-01-01, CC BY 4.0); version 1 of the token index: token_v1/; every correction with its reason: restatements.json
/data/manifests/gpu/<day>.json, /data/manifests/tokens/<day>.json, /data/manifests/index.jsonEach final day's manifest: every file the day was computed from with its SHA-256, the final values, and the SHA-256 of the calculation code
/data/state/<day>.json.gzEach final GPU day's stored state, which the following days' calculation reads
/data/gpu_market.jsonGPUs without a shown index (RTX 5090, RTX 4090, RTX 6000 Ada and others): each one's offers per day at RunPod, Vast.ai, Akash, Shadeform's catalog, Lium, Vultr and the providers outside the index (above), lowest, median and highest price per GPU-hour as posted. Not an index; on Every GPU.
/data/outside.jsonEach indexed GPU's lowest posted on-demand price at each provider outside the index (above), with its offers and memory, read several times a day; a euro price in US dollars at the ECB rate (fx), the euro price in eur. Not in the index; under Other Posted Prices.
/data/token_market.jsonEvery AI model OpenRouter prices for text output: its price, the lowest provider, how many serve it, where to check it (src), its daily prices (series: UTC day, input, output, cache read), carried_from (prices kept when a run could not read them) and refreshed (the last runs). On Every AI model.
/data/token_volume.json, /data/token_spend.jsonEach company's tokens per UTC day on OpenRouter (the token index's weights); their estimated spend at the mix and at list prices, with 30-day totals and a year at that rate
/data/power.jsonDay-ahead wholesale electricity prices at ERCOT's four hubs (from 2017; its yearly hub-price files and daily NP4-190 reports) and the California ISO's SP15, NP15 and ZP26 trading hubs (from August 2023; OASIS): per hub and day, the average of the hourly prices and of the hours ending 7 to 22, in USD per MWh. Not an index; on Wholesale electricity prices.
/data/datacenters.jsonAI data center campuses, curated from the companies' releases and filings: capacity in the company's own measure, users, status with its date and the sources. On AI data center sites.
/data/errata.jsonAny error found in a final value, with the correct figure (or none, when it cannot be recomputed) and the reason (the final value itself is not changed)

The calculation code and a verifier that recomputes any final value from these files, checking each against the day's manifest, are public at github.com/renshuBTC/compute-screener, where a scheduled job runs it on every final day. To check one value: python verify.py --date 2026-10-25 --gpu H100. From 2026-10-28 it first rebuilds each offer's records from the readings (--readings rebuilds any day's records). The code that reads providers' prices is not published.

Governance

Inputs. The GPU index uses posted prices and marketplace asks, which anyone can rent at; executed rentals are not public and can be lower, since large buyers negotiate. Providers weigh equally because rental volumes are not public.

Control. Values are calculated automatically, never set by judgment, and each run must pass automated checks to be published. A GPU index move above 5% in a day is reviewed; a review can only confirm a value or correct an error.

Independence. No provider or company pays to be included, and no link affects the index or the order of providers. Every company the site shows, from price sources and futures venues to AI companies, model hosts and apps, is reviewed for regulator warnings, enforcement actions, fraud reports and security incidents, and again at least every 180 days; a company a source starts listing is reviewed when it first appears. One found to be a scam, or that cannot be identified as a business, is not shown. Compute Screener and its operator hold no futures, swaps or other instruments that settle on GPU rental or AI token prices, and no direct holdings in the providers or companies on this site.

Final values. A value is provisional until its day ends (midnight US Central for GPUs, UTC for tokens), then final; from 2026-10-27 a final value never changes, and each final day has a manifest anyone can recompute (Data). An error found in a final value is recorded with the correct figure and the reason in /data/errata.json and fixed from the next day; the value stays as published. A new method version applies from its start date without recomputing earlier days, except Token Price Index 2.0, which recomputed all token history at the owner's decision and completed it on 2026-10-30 with dated prices found since. Restatements made with GPU versions 4.0 and 4.1 and token version 2.0 are in /data/legacy/restatements.json.

Changes. A material change to the formula, inputs, filters, benchmark contracts or which providers and models count is announced here at least 14 days before it applies, with its version and date; comments to the contact on the Privacy page are summarized with the change. Two changes applied at once, at the owner's decision: GPU version 4.1 (2026-10-24) and Token Price Index 2.0 (2026-10-28). A fix applies from the next day and is announced when made; a new index changes nothing in the others and starts without notice. Current versions: GPU 4.2, from 2026-10-28 (L40S and RTX A6000 indices added; the others unchanged), and Token 2.0, from 2026-10-28.

Third parties. The calculation runs on Cloudflare every minute, with GitHub Actions as a backup several times a day (scheduled every 2 hours, often run late), and the site on Cloudflare Pages. If the ECB rate cannot be read, the last rate up to 7 days old is used, then euro prices are left out. A failing source contributes nothing that run; each source's status is below and on the status page.

Licence. The values and data on this site are licensed CC BY 4.0: anyone may reuse them, including commercially, with credit to "Compute Screener (computescreener.com)" (see the terms). Third-party data keeps its own terms: CC BY 4.0 for GetDeploying and OpenRouter, Apache-2.0 for SkyPilot's catalog.

Continuity. An index that cannot be calculated reliably is not published until it can be. If it stays unpublished for 30 days, or is to be stopped, a notice is published here at least 90 days before it ends, naming any successor; its history stays available under CC BY 4.0.

Questions and complaints go to the contact on the Privacy page: a complaint about a value or the method is acknowledged within 2 business days and answered within 10, and one that leads to a fix or change is summarized here.

IOSCO principles: self-assessment

How the indices meet the 19 IOSCO Principles for Financial Benchmarks (July 2013), assessed by Compute Screener itself, not a third party; gaps are stated.

PrincipleHow it is metGap
1. Overall responsibilityCompute Screener administers both indices: their design, data collection, calculation, publication and governance, all described on this page.One person runs the site; there is no separate legal entity or board.
2. Oversight of third partiesPrices come from providers' public price lists and APIs; the calculation runs on Cloudflare with GitHub Actions as a backup, and the site on Cloudflare Pages (Governance). Each source's status is on the status page.No contracts with the sources: they can change or withdraw their prices at any time.
3. Conflicts of interestNo provider or company pays to be included, and no link affects an index or the order of providers. The administrator holds no instrument that settles on these prices and no direct holding in the providers or companies (Independence).—
4. Control frameworkEvery calculation passes automated checks before it is published; a failed check blocks publication. A GPU index move above 5% in a day is reviewed. Each final day has a checksum manifest.—
5. Internal oversightPublication rules, checks and changes are documented here and in the public verifier.No separate oversight committee. In its place, the data, the calculation code and a verifier are public, and the verifier recomputes every final value daily.
6. Benchmark designEach GPU index prices one benchmark contract (on-demand, 8-GPU node, US), standardizing other configurations to it; each token index is a company's posted prices weighted by its models' usage (GPU Price Index, Token Price Index).Posted prices, not executed rentals (Inputs).
7. Data sufficiencyA GPU value needs at least 5 matched providers, 3 priced that day, so none weighs more than 20%; a token value needs 80% usage coverage. An index without enough data is not published (MI300X today).—
8. Hierarchy of data inputsPrices of offers with capacity come first; a posted price without capacity counts only when its provider had capacity elsewhere; a provider with no price that day is carried from its last reading for up to 7 days, and the share carried is published.Executed transaction prices are not public, so they are not used.
9. Transparency of determinationsEvery price collected (records), what was used or left out and why (trace), and each day's state are published, with a manifest per final day.—
10. Periodic reviewStandardization factors are recalibrated with dated history (model.json); the methodology is reviewed at least once a year, next by October 2027.—
11. Content of the methodologyThis page: definitions, inputs, filters, calculation, imputation, holds, publication rules, finality and governance.—
12. Changes to the methodologyAnnounced here at least 14 days before they apply, with version and date; comments invited and summarized (Changes).Two changes applied at once at the owner's decision: GPU 4.1 and Token 2.0.
13. TransitionAt least 90 days' notice before an index ends, naming a successor if there is one; history stays available (Continuity).—
14. Submitter code of conductNot applicable: no one submits data; prices are collected from public sources.—
15. Controls over data collectionEach source is read on a schedule; parsing, coverage and outlier checks run on every collection, and a failed source contributes nothing that run. Each company shown is reviewed, and again at least every 180 days (Independence).—
16. ComplaintsAcknowledged within 2 business days and answered within 10; complaints leading to a fix or change are summarized here.—
